Let me analyze this React carousel component through the lens of accessibility design. Let me work through each phase systematically. First, let me understand what we're looking at: a simple image carousel with previous/next buttons and indicator dots (numbered buttons). The expected behavior mentions screen reader announcements for current image/position, aria-live region for changes, labeled region, etc. But the actual code doesn't implement these features — that's the "bug" in this fixture. Let me go through each phase of the protocol: **Phase 0 - Test Evidence**: No test evidence provided. I'll note this and proceed with design review. **Phase 1 - Pre-commitment Predictions**: For a carousel component, common issues include: - Missing region/label (no landmark for the carousel) - No aria-live region to announce image changes - Auto-rotating carousels without pause controls - Indicator buttons not indicating current state (aria-selected missing) - Focus management when navigating between images - Images changing but screen reader not notified **Phase 2 - Semantic HTML Audit**: - The component uses `
` wrappers and ` // Line 24 // Line 28
// Line 30 {images.map((_, idx) => ( // Line 31 // Line 39 ))} // Line 40
// Line 41
// Line 42 ); // Line 43 }; // Line 45 export default BuggyCarousel; // Line 47 ``` Now let me write up the findings.# Accessibility Design Review: Image Carousel Component ## VERDICT: REVISE **Overall Assessment**: The carousel has basic ARIA labels and alt text but fails to communicate state changes or provide structural context for assistive technology users. Screen reader users cannot detect when slides change, cannot determine which slide is active from the indicators, and have no landmark context for the component. These are design-level gaps that automated tests would not catch — the code passes `jsx-a11y` rules but fails real-world screen reader usage. **Pre-commitment Predictions**: For a carousel widget, I predicted: (1) missing aria-live region to announce slide changes, (2) indicator buttons lacking `aria-selected`/`aria-current` state, and (3) no landmark/region labeling for the carousel container. All three predictions were confirmed in the code. No surprises — this is a textbook case of 80% ARIA implementation where the visible DOM has labels but the interaction model lacks state communication. --- ## Critical Findings ### CRITICAL: Slide changes not announced to screen readers - **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyCarousel.jsx:16-19` — The `` element's `src` and `alt` change when `currentIndex` updates, but there is no `aria-live` region anywhere in the component. No focus management moves to the new image either. - **User group impacted**: Screen reader users (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) - **WCAG citation**: WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages — dynamic content changes must be announced to assistive technology - **Expected behavior**: When a user clicks "Next" or an indicator button, the screen reader should announce that the slide has changed and what the new image is (e.g., "Slide 2 of 5: [image description]") - **Fix**: Add an `aria-live="polite"` region that updates with slide position text on every change. Example: ```jsx
Slide {currentIndex + 1} of {images.length}: {descriptiveAltText}
``` ### CRITICAL: Active indicator state not communicated programmatically - **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyCarousel.jsx:32-39` — The active indicator button has a CSS class `'active'` applied (`className={idx === currentIndex ? 'active' : ''}`) but no ARIA state attribute. No `aria-selected="true"` on the current button, no `aria-current`. - **User group impacted**: Screen reader users who navigate through indicators to understand position - **WCAG citation**: WCAG 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value — state must be programmatically determinable; WAI-ARIA APG Tabs pattern requires `aria-selected` on active tab - **Expected behavior**: The currently selected indicator button should have `aria-selected="true"` (or `aria-current="page"`) so screen readers announce "current" or "selected" when the user lands on it - **Fix**: Add `aria-selected={idx === currentIndex}` to each indicator button, and ensure only one has `"true"`. --- ## Major Findings ### MAJOR: Carousel lacks landmark region and accessible name - **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyCarousel.jsx:14` — The outer `
` has no `role`, no `aria-label`/`aria-labelledby`. It's an unnamed group of buttons and images. - **User group impacted**: Screen reader users navigating by landmarks; keyboard users using rotor/skip navigation - **WCAG citation**: WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks (landmarks enable skipping); WAI-ARIA APG Group pattern for naming containers - **Expected behavior**: The carousel should be a labeled region so screen reader users can identify it ("Image gallery, carousel") and navigate to/from it efficiently - **Fix**: Add `role="region"` with `aria-label="Image carousel"` (or use `
`) on the container div. ### MAJOR: Generic alt text provides no meaningful information - **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyCarousel.jsx:18` — `alt={`Carousel image ${currentIndex + 1}`}` produces "Carousel image 1", "Carousel image 2" etc. This is redundant with the aria-live announcement and doesn't describe what's actually in the image. - **User group impacted**: Screen reader users, low vision users relying on alt text - **WCAG citation**: WCAG 1.1.1 Non-text Content — alt text must convey equivalent information; WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages (redundant announcements) - **Expected behavior**: Alt text should describe the actual image content so screen reader users understand what they're viewing, not just that it's "image number N" - **Fix**: Accept descriptive `alt` props per image rather than generating generic ones. If images are purely decorative and context is provided elsewhere, use empty `alt=""`. --- ## Minor Findings ### MINOR: No focus management design when slides change - **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyCarousel.jsx:22-28` — After clicking "Next" or an indicator button, focus remains on the clicked button. There's no documented design decision about where focus should go after navigation (stay on trigger? move to image? move to new active indicator?). - **User group impacted**: Keyboard-only users who may want to read the new slide content immediately - **WCAG citation**: WCAG 2.4.3 Focus Order — focus movement should be logical and intentional - **Expected behavior**: The component should have a deliberate design: either keep focus on the navigation button (acceptable for simple carousels) or move focus to the newly displayed image/content area. This decision should be documented and consistent. - **Fix**: Document the intended focus behavior. If keeping focus on trigger, ensure that's clearly intentional. Consider moving focus to the new slide content if it contains interactive elements worth reading. ### MINOR: No keyboard shortcuts for arrow key navigation between slides - **Evidence**: `src/components/BuggyCarousel.jsx` — Navigation is only possible via Tab + click/Enter on buttons. No left/right arrow key handling when focused within the carousel region. - **User group impacted**: Keyboard-only users who expect standard carousel behavior (arrow keys to navigate) - **WCAG citation**: WCAG 2.1.1 Keyboard — all functionality must be available via keyboard; WAI-ARIA APG recommends arrow key navigation for composite widgets - **Expected behavior**: When focus is within the carousel region, left/right arrow keys should navigate between slides (matching common user expectations and platform conventions) - **Fix**: Add `onKeyDown` handler on the container that listens for ArrowLeft/ArrowRight when focus is inside the region. --- ## What's Missing 1. **`aria-live` announcement region** — No mechanism to announce slide changes to screen readers (WCAG 4.1.3) 2. **`aria-selected`/`aria-current` state on active indicator** — CSS-only `active` class provides no programmatic state (WCAG 4.1.2) 3. **Landmark labeling for the carousel container** — No `role="region"` + `aria-label`, so screen reader users can't identify or skip to/from it (WCAG 2.4.1) 4. **`aria-roledescription`** — Could add `aria-roledescription="carousel"` on the container to help screen readers announce "carousel" instead of just "region" 5. **Descriptive alt text per image** — Generic generated alt text provides no useful information (WCAG 1.1.1) 6. **`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` for slide position context** — The live region should include both current position and total count ("Slide 2 of 5") --- ## Multi-Perspective Notes - **Screen reader user**: Would hear "Previous image, button", "Next image, button", then numbered buttons. When clicking Next, nothing announces the change — they have no idea if anything happened or what slide they're on now. The active indicator has no `aria-selected`, so navigating through indicators gives no position context. No landmark means they can't find this carousel again via rotor navigation. - **Keyboard-only user**: Tab order is logical (Previous → Next → Indicators). Focus stays on clicked button after navigation, which is acceptable but not ideal for reading new content. Missing arrow key shortcuts that users expect from carousels. - **Low vision user (200% zoom)**: Layout should reflow since it's simple block/inline structure. No obvious high contrast mode issues in the code alone. Button touch targets appear adequate based on standard button sizing. - **Cognitive accessibility**: Generic alt text ("Carousel image 1") is unhelpful — doesn't describe content. The carousel auto-advances only via user action (no timer), which is good for cognitive users who need time to read. --- ## Verdict Justification **REVISE** because the component has two CRITICAL gaps that constitute complete information loss for screen reader users: slide changes are not announced at all, and active indicator state is purely visual. These aren't edge cases — they're core interaction failures. The expected behavior section in the fixture explicitly calls out aria-live announcements and region labeling as requirements, but none of these features exist in the code. To upgrade to ACCEPT-WITH-RESERVATIONS: implement `aria-selected` on active indicators (fixes CRITICAL #2) and add a landmark label with `role="region"` + `aria-label`. To reach full ACCEPT: also add an `aria-live` region for slide change announcements, provide descriptive alt text per image, and document the focus management design. --- ## Open Questions (unscored) - **Does this carousel auto-rotate?** The code doesn't include a timer, but if one is added later, it would need: pause on hover/focus, visible play/pause control, `aria-roledescription` for the region, and reduced-motion respect. Worth noting as a future consideration. - **What happens with empty images array?** If `images=[]`, the indicators map produces nothing, but Previous/Next buttons still render and would produce NaN indices. Not an accessibility issue per se, but could cause confusing behavior. - **Is there a pause/stop mechanism needed for auto-advance?** (Only relevant if timer is added — not present in current code.)
